title.value: Randomized Trial of Verubecestat for Mild-to-Moderate Alzheimer’s Disease
title.quote:
Randomized Trial of Verubecestat for Mild-to-Moderate Alzheimer’s Disease
**Authors:** Michael F. Egan, James Kost, Pierre N. Tariot, Paul S. Aisen
title.location: Title line and author line at the head of the document

design.value: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 78-week trial period (part 1), followed by an optional extension period (part 2) of up to 5 years
design.quote: The trial consisted of a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 78-week trial period (part 1), followed by an optional extension period with a total planned duration of up to 5 years (part 2).

phase.value: phase 2 lead-in safety cohort component intended to transition to a phase 3 trial
phase.quote: Part 1 was designed to include a phase 2 lead-in safety cohort component that was intended to transition to a phase 3 trial if satisfactory safety results were observed.

n.quote: A total of 1958 patients underwent randomization; 653 were randomly assigned to receive verubecestat at a dose of 12 mg per day (the 12-mg group)

n_description.value: 1958 patients underwent randomization and were included in the primary population: 653 assigned to verubecestat 12 mg/day, 652 to verubecestat 40 mg/day, and 653 to matching placebo
n_description.quote: A total of 1958 patients were included in the primary population; 653 were randomly assigned to receive verubecestat at a dose of 12 mg per day (the 12-mg group)

population.value: patients between 55 and 85 years of age who met standard research and clinical criteria for dementia probably due to Alzheimer's disease, with an entry Mini-Mental State Examination score of 15 to 26 (mild or moderate dementia)
population.quote: Patients were eligible for enrollment in the trial if they were between 55 and 85 years of age and if they met standard research and clinical criteria for dementia that was probably due to Alzheimer’s disease.

followup.value: 78-week double-blind treatment period (part 1); an optional extension period (part 2) of up to 5 years was planned but no patient completed it
followup.quote: The trial consisted of a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 78-week trial period (part 1), followed by an optional extension period with a total planned duration of up to 5 years (part 2).

intervention.value: oral verubecestat 12 mg or 40 mg once daily; a 60-mg dose level was included only in the phase 2 lead-in safety cohort and was prespecified to be dropped for the phase 3 component
intervention.quote: In the phase 2 lead-in safety period, patients were randomly assigned to receive, once daily, one of three oral dose levels of verubecestat (12 mg, 40 mg, or 60 mg) or placebo.

comparator.value: matching placebo (653 patients), administered as identical-appearing tablets
comparator.quote: 652 to receive verubecestat at a dose of 40 mg per day (the 40-mg group), and 653 to receive matching placebo.

biomarker_confirmation.value: None required for entry — the trial did not require the presence of an amyloid biomarker at screening; PET amyloid and cerebrospinal fluid biomarker substudies were conducted in subsets and showed approximately 90% of patients met criteria for Alzheimer's disease

funding: The sponsor (Merck) designed the trial in consultation with the academic authors.
limitations: A limitation of our trial was the lack of requirement for the presence of an amyloid biomarker at screening, thereby potentially allowing patients who had dementia owing to nonamyloid-related disease to be included.

Bias may have been introduced in the uncontrolled selection of patients for the biomarker substudies, but the demographic characteristics of these patients were similar to those of the overall population of the trial.
Although subgroup analyses that were based on patient characteristics were prespecified, the trial was not adequately powered for such analyses.

Sensitivity analyses that were planned to explore the results of the efficacy analyses under the assumption that data were not missing at random were not performed given the negative results of the trial.
The trial was terminated early for futility 50 months after onset, which was within 5 months before its scheduled completion, and after enrollment of the planned 1958 patients was complete.
Similar reductions have been reported with other antiamyloid therapies, and the clinical significance of this finding is unknown.

risk_of_bias.judgement: Data were collected by the investigators but analyzed by the sponsor (Merck), which also designed the trial and funded it.

risk_of_bias.judgement: The first manuscript draft was written by a medical writer employed by the sponsor together with the first author.

risk_of_bias.judgement: Roughly 30% of randomized patients did not complete the 78-week part 1, and premature withdrawal for adverse events was more frequent in both verubecestat groups than in placebo.
risk_of_bias.quote: A total of 1389 patients (70.2 to 72.1% of the patients in each group) completed part 1 of the trial

risk_of_bias.judgement: The trial was stopped by the data and safety monitoring committee for futility in February 2017, 5 months before the scheduled completion of part 1, and no patient completed part 2.
risk_of_bias.quote: The decision to stop the trial was made in February 2017 at the recommendation of the independent data and safety monitoring committee on the basis of futility

risk_of_bias.judgement: Planned not-missing-at-random sensitivity analyses were abandoned because the trial was negative, so the robustness of the efficacy analyses to missing data was not examined.
risk_of_bias.quote: Sensitivity analyses that were planned to explore the results of the efficacy analyses under the assumption that data were not missing at random were not performed given the negative results of the trial.

risk_of_bias.judgement: No amyloid biomarker was required at screening, so patients with non-amyloid dementia could enter; the authors argue substudy data make this unlikely to explain the result.
risk_of_bias.quote: A limitation of our trial was the lack of requirement for the presence of an amyloid biomarker at screening, thereby potentially allowing patients who had dementia owing to nonamyloid-related disease to be included.

risk_of_bias.judgement: Routine MRI monitoring for amyloid-related imaging abnormalities was discontinued partway through the trial, so ARIA ascertainment was incomplete and no ARIA counts are reported.

risk_of_bias.judgement: Patients were not randomly selected into the PET amyloid and cerebrospinal fluid substudies; participation depended on site willingness and proximity to a PET ligand facility.
risk_of_bias.quote: Bias may have been introduced in the uncontrolled selection of patients for the biomarker substudies, but the demographic characteristics of these patients were similar to those of the overall population of the trial.

risk_of_bias.domain: post-randomization exclusions from the analysed population
risk_of_bias.judgement: The first 200 patients enrolled and the 53 patients assigned to the 60-mg dose were excluded from the primary efficacy and safety analyses.
risk_of_bias.quote: The efficacy analyses were performed in the primary population, which included all patients who underwent randomization except the first 200 patients enrolled in the study and the patients who were randomly assigned to receive the 60-mg dose of verubecestat.

disagreements.question: Does the amyloid hypothesis hold once Alzheimer's dementia is clinically established?
disagreements.position: This trial concludes that near-maximal BACE-1 inhibition for 78 weeks did not slow clinical progression, which suggests either that progression is independent of A-beta production once dementia is present or that the amyloid hypothesis may not be correct.
disagreements.attributed_to: the authors of this trial (Egan et al., New England Journal of Medicine)
disagreements.quote: This suggests that once dementia is present, disease progression may be independent of A β production or, alternatively, that the amyloid hypothesis of Alzheimer’s disease may not be correct.

disagreements.question: Do antiamyloid drugs necessarily cause amyloid-related imaging abnormalities?
disagreements.position: Verubecestat, a BACE-1 inhibitor, was not found to be associated with the ARIA seen with some other antiamyloid therapies.
disagreements.attributed_to: the authors of this trial (Egan et al., New England Journal of Medicine)
disagreements.quote: However, verubecestat was not found to be associated with the amyloid-related imaging abnormalities that have been observed with some other antiamyloid therapies.

disagreements.question: Could an inadequate dose explain the negative result?
disagreements.position: No — CSF A-beta was reduced by 63 to 81%, confirming target engagement, and phase 1 modeling indicated a 60-mg dose would not be substantially more effective than 40 mg.
disagreements.attributed_to: the authors of this trial (Egan et al., New England Journal of Medicine)
disagreements.quote: On the basis of pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic modeling in phase 1 studies, a 60-mg dose of verubecestat was not substantially more effective than a 40-mg dose in reducing the A β concentration in cerebrospinal fluid.

disagreements.question: Could enrollment of patients without amyloid pathology explain the negative result?
disagreements.position: No — approximately 90% of substudy patients had findings consistent with Alzheimer's disease and about 63% were APOE4 carriers, so the non-amyloid proportion was probably small.
disagreements.attributed_to: the authors of this trial (Egan et al., New England Journal of Medicine)
disagreements.quote: Taken together, these observations suggest that the proportion of patients without amyloid-related disease who were included in the trial was probably small and unlikely to account for the negative results.

disagreements.question: What does the greater hippocampal volume loss under verubecestat mean?
disagreements.position: The document reports greater hippocampal volume reduction with verubecestat than placebo, notes similar reductions with other antiamyloid therapies, and states the clinical significance is unknown rather than adjudicating it.
disagreements.attributed_to: the authors of this trial (Egan et al., New England Journal of Medicine)
disagreements.quote: The reduction in hippocampal volume at week 78 was greater in the verubecestat groups than in the placebo group.

disagreements.question: When should amyloid-targeting treatment be given?
disagreements.position: The document endorses the proposal that amyloid-targeting treatment should be given early, before the onset of clinical symptoms.
disagreements.attributed_to: the authors of this trial (Egan et al., New England Journal of Medicine), citing a prior proposal
disagreements.quote: Because A β deposition takes place years before clinical symptoms become apparent, it has been proposed that treatments targeting amyloid should be implemented early in the disease process, before the onset of clinical symptoms.
